Hi all — quick answers to the two asks below.

1) Token billing behaviour: Hosted API bills strictly on token counts per request with standard tokenization (utf8 BPE). We aggregate tokens separately for input and output and report both lines on invoices. Rounding: we do not round to the nearest 1K tokens for billing; we bill exact token counts prorated to the per‑1M price (i.e., cost = (tokens / 1,000,000) * unit_price). Edge case: streaming responses that are aborted still incur output tokens generated.

2) Hosted vs Dedicated parity & recommendation: Our hosted catalog exposes the same model families as Dedicated but hosted variants are tuned for multi‑tenant latency profiles. For low‑latency chat at pilot scale we recommend rwd-chat‑small‑v2 (hosted) — it gives sub‑200ms token latency in our US‑west regions at small batch sizes. If you move embeddings to a Dedicated instance for batch throughput, rwd-embed‑dense‑v1 is bit‑compatible with hosted outputs; expect identical embedding vectors between hosted and dedicated runs when using the same quantization flags.

Pilot discount note (for Tessa to forward): we can commit a one‑time pilot rebate off list (applied as a credit) for month 1; formal volume tiers start at 10M tokens/mo.

Happy to jump on a quick 15m call if you want us to walk procurement through a one‑pager.
